plain_6parts.title: Part 1 of 6 — Background and global conventions
plain_6parts.text:
Implement a small reconciliation tool for an e-commerce settlement team. Each day, the team exports one mixed text file containing both order and payment records. The tool parses the file, matches payments to orders, and produces a summary.

The following conventions apply everywhere:

- Store and calculate every monetary amount internally as an integer number of cents. For example, `"12.30"` becomes `1230`.
- Silently skip records that cannot be parsed or do not satisfy the format. Do not raise an exception and do not print a warning.
- Process only records whose currency is exactly `USD` after surrounding whitespace is removed. Treat every other currency as invalid.
- Treat every timestamp as UTC. Do not perform timezone conversion.

plain_6parts.title: Part 2 of 6 — Data format
plain_6parts.text:
The input contains one record per line. Every line has exactly six fields separated by `|`:

```text
TYPE|RECORD_ID|ORDER_ID|AMOUNT|CURRENCY|TIMESTAMP
```

- `TYPE` is `ORDER` or `PAYMENT`, matched without regard to case and normalised to uppercase.
- Trim surrounding whitespace from both identifiers. Both must then be non-empty. For an `ORDER`, `RECORD_ID` and `ORDER_ID` must be equal.
- `AMOUNT` is an ordinary decimal string with at most three fractional digits. It may contain only digits and at most one decimal point, with an optional leading minus sign; scientific notation and every other numeric notation are invalid. Round a third fractional digit to cents using round-half-up; more than three fractional digits is invalid. A negative `PAYMENT` is a refund. A negative `ORDER` is invalid.
- `TIMESTAMP` must have the exact format `2024-03-15 14:30`. Invalid calendar values or other formats are invalid.
- If the same trimmed `RECORD_ID` occurs more than once, retain the first valid occurrence and skip later occurrences.

A parsed record is an ordinary dictionary, never a tuple. It has exactly the keys `"type"`, `"record_id"`, `"order_id"`, `"amount"`, `"currency"`, and `"timestamp"`; fields are read by those key names, for example `record["type"]`. `amount` is integer cents, `currency` is `"USD"`, and `timestamp` is a naive Python `datetime` representing UTC.

plain_6parts.title: Part 3 of 6 — Summary report
Part 4 of 6 — Payment matching
plain_6parts.text:
`match_payments(records)` associates payments with orders by `order_id`.

- A non-refund payment qualifies only when its timestamp is at or after the order timestamp and no later than exactly 72 hours after it. Both endpoints are included.
- If several payments qualify, use the one with the earliest timestamp. Break an exact timestamp tie by retained source order.
- Negative payments are refunds and never qualify as matched payments.
- Return one result for every order, following retained order-record order. Each result is an ordinary dictionary, never a tuple, with exactly `"order_id"`, `"status"`, and `"amount"`. Read these fields by key name, for example `result["order_id"]`. Status is exactly lowercase `"matched"` or `"unmatched"`. An unmatched result has amount `0`.

plain_6parts.title: Part 5 of 6 — Parsing and loading functions
plain_6parts.text:
- `parse_amount(s)` returns integer cents for a valid amount string and `None` otherwise. It follows the syntax, precision, and round-half-up rules in Part 2. A non-string input is invalid and returns `None`.
- `parse_record(line)` returns the exact parsed-record dictionary described in Part 2, or `None` when any field is invalid.
- `load_records(text)` parses all lines, silently skips invalid lines, and applies the first-valid-record duplicate rule. An invalid occurrence does not reserve its record ID.
- `compute_refunds(records)` returns the positive sum, in cents, of the absolute values of all negative `PAYMENT` amounts. A refund counts even if no order with its `order_id` exists.

None of these functions mutates an input object, prints output, or stores global state.

plain_6parts.title: Part 6 of 6 — Release clarification
plain_6parts.text:
The released calculation changes one sentence in Part 3: `net_total` must subtract `refund_total`. It is therefore the sum of matched payment amounts minus the positive refund total. This clarification overrides only the earlier statement that refunds were not included.

After trimming, an empty record ID is invalid. The order IDs placed in `unmatched_ids` are the same already-trimmed IDs stored in parsed records.

- `"unmatched_ids"`: unmatched order IDs in ascending lexicographic order.

Every item in `matches` is the result dictionary specified in Part 3, not a tuple. The exact key spellings and the lowercase status value described later are part of the contract. A release clarification in Part 5 may override one detail in this initial rule.

reference_steps.title: Step 1 of 6 — Implement parse_amount(s)
reference_steps.text: Convert an amount string to an integer number of cents, so 12.30 becomes 1230. The input must be a string containing only digits and at most one decimal point, with an optional leading minus sign; scientific notation and every other numeric notation are invalid. One or two fractional digits are scaled normally. A third fractional digit is rounded to cents using round-half-up, including for negative values; more than three fractional digits is invalid. Return None for malformed, non-string, or non-finite input. Negative amounts remain negative at this stage because a negative PAYMENT represents a refund, while a negative ORDER is rejected in the next step.

reference_steps.title: Step 2 of 6 — Implement parse_record(line)
reference_steps.text: Parse one line containing exactly six | separated fields in this order: TYPE, RECORD_ID, ORDER_ID, AMOUNT, CURRENCY, TIMESTAMP. TYPE is case-insensitive ORDER or PAYMENT and is stored uppercase. Trim both identifiers and reject the line if either becomes empty. An ORDER requires equal record and order IDs and cannot have a negative amount; a negative PAYMENT is valid. Apply all parse_amount rules to AMOUNT. CURRENCY must be exactly USD after trimming. TIMESTAMP must use the exact format 2024-03-15 14:30 and represents UTC without conversion. Return None for any invalid field without raising or printing. Otherwise return an ordinary dictionary, never a tuple, with exactly type, record_id, order_id, amount, currency, and timestamp. Read fields by key name, for example record["type"]. amount is integer cents and timestamp is a naive Python datetime.

reference_steps.title: Step 3 of 6 — Implement load_records(text)
reference_steps.text: Parse the input one line at a time with parse_record and preserve retained source order. Silently skip every invalid line. Compare record IDs after trimming. For a repeated record ID, retain the first valid occurrence and skip later valid occurrences; an invalid occurrence does not reserve that ID. Return an empty list for non-string or empty input. Do not mutate inputs, print output, or store global state.

reference_steps.title: Step 4 of 6 — Implement compute_refunds(records)
reference_steps.text: A refund is any PAYMENT record whose integer-cent amount is negative. Return the positive sum of the absolute amounts of all refunds. A refund counts even when no order has the same order ID. Non-negative payments and ORDER records contribute nothing, and no refund returns 0. Do not mutate records or store global state.

reference_steps.title: Step 5 of 6 — Implement match_payments(records)
reference_steps.text: Produce one result for every ORDER, following retained order-record order. Associate non-negative PAYMENT records by order_id. A payment qualifies only when its timestamp is at or after the order timestamp and no later than exactly 72 hours afterward; both endpoints are included. If several payments qualify, choose the earliest timestamp and break an exact timestamp tie by retained source order. Negative payments are refunds and never match. Each result is an ordinary dictionary, never a tuple, with exactly order_id, status, and amount. Read fields by key name, for example result["order_id"]. Status is exactly lowercase matched or unmatched. A matched result uses the chosen payment amount; an unmatched result uses amount 0.

reference_steps.title: Step 6 of 6 — Implement build_summary(matches, refund_total)
reference_steps.text: Every item in matches is the result dictionary from Step 5, never a tuple; read order_id, status, and amount by their exact key names. Return a dictionary with exactly four keys. total_orders is len(matches). matched_count counts results whose status is exactly lowercase matched. net_total follows the released rule: sum the amounts of matched results and subtract the positive refund_total; this overrides the earlier draft that excluded refunds. unmatched_ids contains the already-trimmed order_id from every result whose status is exactly lowercase unmatched, sorted in ascending lexicographic order. With empty matches, the counts are 0, unmatched_ids is empty, and net_total still subtracts refund_total.

formal_gpt4o_01.title: Step 1 of 6 — Parse the monetary amount
formal_gpt4o_01.text:
Implement `parse_amount(s)` to convert a monetary string to integer cents.
- Accept a string `s` that represents an amount with at most three fractional digits.
- Return integer cents, applying round-half-up for a third fractional digit.
- Skip any format other than ordinary decimal with up to one decimal point.
- Negative values are valid for `PAYMENT` only; handle accordingly.
- Return `None` for any invalid string or if `s` is not a string.

formal_gpt4o_01.title: Step 2 of 6 — Parse and validate a record
formal_gpt4o_01.text:
Implement `parse_record(line)` to convert a line into a dictionary.
- Line format: `TYPE|RECORD_ID|ORDER_ID|AMOUNT|CURRENCY|TIMESTAMP`.
- Normalize `TYPE` to uppercase and ensure `RECORD_ID`, `ORDER_ID` are not empty post-trimming.
- For `ORDER`, ensure `RECORD_ID` equals `ORDER_ID`.
- Only accept records with currency `USD` after trimming whitespace.
- Convert `TIMESTAMP` to naive `datetime` if format is `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`.
- Use `parse_amount(s)` for `AMOUNT`, ensuring it is positive for `ORDER`.
- Return `None` if any field is invalid or does not meet the rule.

formal_gpt4o_01.title: Step 3 of 6 — Load and deduplicate records
formal_gpt4o_01.text:
Implement `load_records(text)` to process multiline input.
- Split `text` into lines; each line attempts parsing with `parse_record(line)`.
- Silently skip lines that return `None`.
- Ensure only the first occurrence of a `RECORD_ID` is retained, discarding others.

formal_gpt4o_01.title: Step 4 of 6 — Compute total refunds
formal_gpt4o_01.text:
Implement `compute_refunds(records)` to calculate the refund total.
- Iterate through `records`, identifying `PAYMENT` with negative `AMOUNT`.
- Sum absolute values of negative `AMOUNTs`, returning their positive sum.
- Refund calculation includes payments with no corresponding `order_id`.

formal_gpt4o_01.title: Step 5 of 6 — Match payments to orders
formal_gpt4o_01.text:
Implement `match_payments(records)` to associate valid `PAYMENTs` to `ORDERs`.
- Ensure a non-refund `PAYMENT` timestamp is between `ORDER` timestamp and 72 hours later.
- In case of multiple `PAYMENTs`, select the earliest timestamp, breaking ties by source order.
- Only return matched `PAYMENTs` as `'{"status": "matched" ...}`. An unmatched order is `'amount': 0`.
- Return one dictionary per `ORDER`, maintaining input order.

formal_gpt4o_01.title: Step 6 of 6 — Build reconciliation summary
formal_gpt4o_01.text:
Implement `build_summary(matches, refund_total)` to produce reconciliation summary.
- `total_orders` captures the number of valid `ORDERs`.
- `matched_count` is the number of matched `ORDERs`.
- `net_total` sums matched `PAYMENTs`, **subtracting `refund_total`.**
- `unmatched_ids` lists lexicographically sorted unmatched `ORDER_IDs`.

formal_gpt4o_02.title: Step 1 of 6 — Parse Amount
formal_gpt4o_02.text:
Implement `parse_amount(s)` to convert a valid amount string to integer cents.
- Accept a string with an ordinary decimal string with at most three fractional digits.
- The string can contain only digits, one optional decimal point, and an optional leading minus sign.
- Round a third fractional digit to cents using **round-half-up**.
- Return `None` for non-string inputs or invalid strings (e.g., containing letters or more than one decimal point).
- Ensure the function handles edge cases such as `".50"` yielding `50` cents.

formal_gpt4o_02.title: Step 2 of 6 — Parse Record
formal_gpt4o_02.text:
Create `parse_record(line)` to parse a line of records into a dictionary or return `None` if invalid.
- Split the input line by '|', expecting exactly six fields.
- Normalize `TYPE` to uppercase and trim whitespace from all fields.
- Ensure `RECORD_ID` and `ORDER_ID` are non-empty after trimming.
- For an `ORDER`, verify `RECORD_ID` equals `ORDER_ID`.
- Parse `AMOUNT` using `parse_amount(s)` and ensure the amount is non-negative for `ORDER` types.
- Validate `CURRENCY` is exactly `USD`.
- Ensure `TIMESTAMP` is formatted as `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM"`.
- Return `None` for any field violations.

formal_gpt4o_02.title: Step 3 of 6 — Load Records
formal_gpt4o_02.text:
Implement `load_records(text)` to parse lines of text into valid records, ignoring duplicates and invalid lines.
- Split the `text` input into lines and apply `parse_record(line)` on each.
- Silently skip lines that return `None` from parsing.
- Retain only the first valid occurrence of each `RECORD_ID`.
- Return a list of parsed dictionary records.

formal_gpt4o_02.title: Step 4 of 6 — Compute Refunds
formal_gpt4o_02.text:
Develop `compute_refunds(records)` to calculate the sum of absolute values of negative payments.
- Iterate over parsed records, checking for `PAYMENT` type.
- Sum the absolute `amount` of records with negative `PAYMENT` amounts.
- Return the total refund amount in positive cents.
- Include a refund even if no order with its `order_id` exists.

formal_gpt4o_02.title: Step 5 of 6 — Match Payments
formal_gpt4o_02.text:
Create `match_payments(records)` to pair payments with orders based on `order_id`.
- Match `PAYMENT` with `ORDER` only if `PAYMENT` timestamp is within [order timestamp, order timestamp + 72 hours].
- Select the earliest valid `PAYMENT`, breaking ties by source order.
- Ignore negative `amount` payments as they are considered refunds.
- Return a list of results each as a dictionary with keys: `"order_id"`, `"status"`, and `"amount"`. Use lowercase `"matched"` or `"unmatched"` for status.
- A matched order includes `amount`, unmatched has `amount` 0.

formal_gpt4o_02.title: Step 6 of 6 — Build Summary
formal_gpt4o_02.text:
Implement `build_summary(matches, refund_total)` to create a summary dictionary of the reconciliation process.
- Include `"total_orders"` as the total count of valid orders.
- Include `"matched_count"` as the count of matched payments.
- Calculate `"net_total"` as the sum of matched payment amounts minus the positive refund total.
- List `"unmatched_ids"` as unmatched `order_id`s sorted lexicographically.
- Ensure output is a dictionary matching the expected key names and format.

formal_gpt4o_03.title: Step 1 of 6 — Parse Amount Strings
formal_gpt4o_03.text:
Develop the `parse_amount(s)` function to convert a string representing a monetary amount to integer cents.
- Inputs: a string `s` that may contain a decimal number representing dollars and cents.
- Outputs: an integer representing the amount in cents if valid, or `None` if invalid.
- The string can have at most three fractional digits, requiring rounding to cents using round-half-up if there are three fractional digits.
- The string can include digits and one decimal point, with an optional leading minus sign.
- Return `None` for all invalid strings and non-string inputs.
- **Store every monetary amount internally as an integer number of cents.**

formal_gpt4o_03.title: Step 2 of 6 — Parse Individual Record Lines
formal_gpt4o_03.text:
Implement the `parse_record(line)` function to parse a single record line into a dictionary or return `None` if invalid.
- Inputs: a line of text structured as `TYPE|RECORD_ID|ORDER_ID|AMOUNT|CURRENCY|TIMESTAMP`.
- Outputs: a dictionary with the fields parsed into the keys `type`, `record_id`, `order_id`, `amount`, `currency`, `timestamp`, or `None` if the record is invalid.
- `TYPE` should be `ORDER` or `PAYMENT`, normalized to uppercase. `RECORD_ID` and `ORDER_ID` must be trimmed and non-empty, and equal for `ORDER`.
- `AMOUNT` must be converted to integer cents using `parse_amount` function. An `ORDER` with a negative `AMOUNT` is invalid.
- Only process records with `CURRENCY` exactly as `USD`, trimming surrounding whitespace.
- `TIMESTAMP` format must be `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`. Treat it as a naive UTC `datetime` if valid.

formal_gpt4o_03.title: Step 3 of 6 — Load and Filter All Records
formal_gpt4o_03.text:
Create the `load_records(text)` function to process multiple record lines.
- Input: a multi-line string `text` where each line is a record.
- Output: a list of parsed record dictionaries for valid records, after applying the first-valid-record duplicate rule.
- Silently skip records that cannot be parsed or don't meet format requirements.
- **Retain only the first valid occurrence of each `RECORD_ID`, ignore subsequent occurrences.**
- An invalid occurrence does not reserve its `RECORD_ID`.

formal_gpt4o_03.title: Step 4 of 6 — Calculate Refund Totals
formal_gpt4o_03.text:
Develop `compute_refunds(records)` to sum the absolute values of negative `PAYMENT` amounts.
- Input: a list of parsed record dictionaries.
- Output: the total sum in cents of the absolute values of negative `PAYMENT` amounts.
- Include refunds even if there are no matching orders by `order_id`.
- Sum must be positive as positive refund total is subtracted in later calculations.

formal_gpt4o_03.title: Step 5 of 6 — Match Payments to Orders
formal_gpt4o_03.text:
Create the `match_payments(records)` function to associate payments with orders.
- Input: a list of parsed record dictionaries.
- Output: a list of result dictionaries with `order_id`, `status`, and `amount`. `status` is `matched` or `unmatched`.
- A payment matches an order if it's non-negative, with a timestamp at/after the order's one and within 72 hours.
- Use the earliest qualifying payment by timestamp and retained order if ties exist.
- Return results following the order-record order. `Unmatched` results have amount `0`.

formal_gpt4o_03.title: Step 6 of 6 — Generate Final Summary
formal_gpt4o_03.text:
Implement `build_summary(matches, refund_total)` to create a summary dictionary.
- Inputs: `matches` list from `match_payments` and `refund_total` from `compute_refunds`.
- Output: a dictionary with `total_orders`, `matched_count`, `net_total`, and `unmatched_ids`.
- `total_orders` is the count of valid orders processed.
- `matched_count` is the count of results with status `matched`.
- **`net_total` is the sum of matched payments minus `refund_total`.**
- `unmatched_ids` contains all unmatched order IDs in ascending lexicographic order.
- Net total calculation was clarified to include refund subtraction.

formal_gpt4o_04.title: Step 1 of 6 — Parse Amount Strings
formal_gpt4o_04.text:
Implement `parse_amount(s)` to convert a valid amount string to integer cents.
- It receives a string `s` that represents a monetary amount in USD.
- The string must be a valid decimal number with at most three fractional digits.
- Convert the amount recorded in dollars and cents to an integer number of cents.
- Use **round-half-up** if there is a third fractional digit.
- Return `None` for any non-string input or string with more than three fractional digits.

formal_gpt4o_04.title: Step 2 of 6 — Parse a Single Record Line
formal_gpt4o_04.text:
Create the `parse_record(line)` function to convert a valid record from a text line into a dictionary.
- Input is a text `line` containing six fields separated by `|`.
- Fields are `TYPE|RECORD_ID|ORDER_ID|AMOUNT|CURRENCY|TIMESTAMP`.
- `TYPE` should be `ORDER` or `PAYMENT` and normalized to uppercase.
- `RECORD_ID` and `ORDER_ID` are trimmed of whitespace and must be non-empty. For `ORDER`, they must be equal.
- `AMOUNT` must be converted to integer cents using `parse_amount()`.
- `CURRENCY` should be exactly `USD` after trimming surrounding whitespace.
- `TIMESTAMP` must follow the exact format `2024-03-15 14:30`.
- Return a dictionary or `None` if any field is invalid.

formal_gpt4o_04.title: Step 3 of 6 — Load Records into a List
formal_gpt4o_04.text:
Create the `load_records(text)` function to parse multiple lines of records from a text blob.
- Input is `text`, a string containing multiple lines.
- Use `parse_record(line)` to parse each line.
- **Silently skip** lines that are invalid or whose record IDs are duplicates (retain the first valid occurrence).
- Maintain the order of the first valid occurrence recovered from `text`.

formal_gpt4o_04.title: Step 4 of 6 — Match Payments to Orders
formal_gpt4o_04.text:
Implement `match_payments(records)` to associate payments with orders by `order_id`.
- Input `records` is a list of dictionaries returned by `load_records`.
- A payment qualifies if its timestamp is ≥ the order timestamp and ≤ 72 hours later.
- Use the earliest qualifying payment by timestamp; resolve ties by original order in input.
- **Negative payments** are refunds and never qualify as matched payments.
- Return one result dictionary for each order: `"order_id"`, `"status"` (`"matched"` or `"unmatched"`), and the total `"amount"`. Amount is 0 if unmatched.

formal_gpt4o_04.title: Step 5 of 6 — Compute Total Refunds
formal_gpt4o_04.text:
Implement `compute_refunds(records)` to calculate the total refunds.
- Input is `records`, a list generated by `load_records`.
- Sum the absolute values of all negative `PAYMENT` amounts.
- Return the positive sum, in integer cents, even if no order matches these refunds.

formal_gpt4o_04.title: Step 6 of 6 — Build Summary of Results
formal_gpt4o_04.text:
Create `build_summary(matches, refund_total)` to generate a summary dictionary.
- `matches` is a list of result dictionaries from `match_payments`.
- `refund_total` is the total sum of refunds in cents computed by `compute_refunds`.
- Return a dictionary with keys: `"total_orders"`, `"matched_count"`, `"net_total"`, and `"unmatched_ids"`.
- Calculate `"net_total"` as the sum of matched payments minus `refund_total`.
- `"unmatched_ids"` should list unmatched order IDs in ascending order.

formal_gpt4o_05.title: Step 1 of 6 — Parse and convert amount
formal_gpt4o_05.text:
Implement `parse_amount(s)` to handle amount conversion and validation.
- Convert a valid decimal string to integer cents by removing the decimal point and adjusting if necessary.
- Round any fractional part to cents using **round-half-up** if three digits are present, otherwise directly convert.
- Return `None` for inputs with more than three fractional digits or invalid format (e.g., letters or scientific notation).
- A non-string input or malformed string also results in `None`.

formal_gpt4o_05.title: Step 2 of 6 — Parse a single record
formal_gpt4o_05.text:
Create `parse_record(line)` to parse a line of input into a dictionary.
- Split the line by `|` into exactly six fields.
- The `TYPE` field must be uppercased `ORDER` or `PAYMENT`.
- `RECORD_ID` and `ORDER_ID` must match for an `ORDER` and be non-empty after trimming whitespace.
- Use `parse_amount` to convert `AMOUNT`, and ensure it is valid and non-negative for `ORDER`.
- `CURRENCY` must exactly match `USD` with whitespace trimmed.
- The `TIMESTAMP` must follow the exact format `2024-03-15 14:30`.
- Return a dictionary with the valid fields or `None` for any invalid field.

formal_gpt4o_05.title: Step 3 of 6 — Load all records from text
formal_gpt4o_05.text:
Define `load_records(text)` to handle parsing all lines from input and managing duplicates.
- Split input text into lines and parse each line with `parse_record`.
- Silently skip invalid lines without exceptions or warnings.
- Keep the first occurrence when a `record_id` is duplicated; skip later ones.
- Gather and return a list of valid records as dictionaries.

formal_gpt4o_05.title: Step 4 of 6 — Compute refund totals
formal_gpt4o_05.text:
Implement `compute_refunds(records)` to compute the sum of refunds.
- Iterate over `records` to identify negative `PAYMENT` amounts, classified as refunds.
- Compute the positive **sum** of the absolute values of these refunds in cents.
- Return the calculated refund total. Refunds are included regardless of existing orders.

formal_gpt4o_05.title: Step 5 of 6 — Match payments to orders
